\section[leider]{leider — unfortunately}

\label{lesson:GE-C172-leider}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the German for before, then the German for later.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: leider}
\textbf{leider} — \textquotedblleft{}unfortunately\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{leider} $\leftarrow$ Old High German \emph{leidir} (EtymDB 2.1), a form of the word for \textquotedblleft{}sorrow, harm\textquotedblright{}, which EtymDB lists beside English \emph{loath}: \textquotedblleft{}sadly\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[vielleicht]{vielleicht — perhaps}

\label{lesson:GE-C172-vielleicht}

Before the new one: say the German for later, then the German for unfortunately.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: vielleicht}
\textbf{vielleicht} — \textquotedblleft{}perhaps\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{vielleicht} $\leftarrow$ Middle High German \emph{vil līhte}, \textquotedblleft{}very easily\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB 2.1): \emph{viel} + \emph{leicht}. What could very easily happen is what perhaps will.
\end{cousinweb}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: wahrscheinlich}
\textbf{wahrscheinlich} — \textquotedblleft{}probably\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{wahrscheinlich} is the word for \textquotedblleft{}true\textquotedblright{}, Old High German \emph{wār}, + the word for \textquotedblleft{}appearance, shine\textquotedblright{}, English \emph{shine} (EtymDB 2.1), + \emph{-lich}: \textquotedblleft{}true-seeming\textquotedblright{}, a copy of Latin \emph{vērisimilis}.
\end{cousinweb}

\textbf{natürlich} — \textquotedblleft{}of course\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}

\end{cousinweb}
